messages.author: ed8d9f4a4c19d66c
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in Part 2 - non-numeric argument
parts:
Dear Vincent,

Thank you for getting back to me.

The script that I used to run part 1 and 2 ( apologies for all the notes). How can I share the R file with you? The file is too big. 

  f0=1,
  f1=1,
  overwrite = TRUE,#Overwrite previously generated milestone data by this function for this particular dataset. 
  #If FALSE then it will skip the previously processed files (default=FALSE).
  do.imp=TRUE,
  idloc=1,#default=1 which assumes participant ID number is in the accelerometer file header; if no ID is extracted in the
  #output report, try idloc=2 (particularly for ActiGraph files); tells GGIR where to find the participant ID (default: inside file header)
  print.filename=TRUE,
  storefolderstructure=TRUE,
  windowsizes = c(1,900,3600),#5 s epoch, 15 min non-wear detection resolution, 60 min non-wear evaluation window
  do.cal=TRUE,
  do.anglez=TRUE,
  do.enmo = TRUE,
  do.mad=FALSE,
  do.hfen=FALSE,
  do.en=FALSE,
  chunksize=1,
  printsummary=TRUE,
  
  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  strategy = 1, #see manual p43; '2'=only data between 1st & last midnight used for imputation
  hrs.del.start = 1, #needed if 'strategy'=1; how many hours after start of data collection did wearing of  monitor start?
  hrs.del.end = 1, #needed if 'strategy'=1;how many hours before end of data collection did wearing of monitor end?
  maxdur = 9, #maximum number of days you expect in a data file based on the study protocol; how many 24h windows after start of data recording did data collection end; 0 is default if unknown 
  #max_calendar_days = 8, #the number of calendar days after start of data recording did data collection end
  ndayswindow=7, #used if 'strategy'=3; it is size of the window as number of days
  includedaycrit = 16, #minimum number of valid hours/day
  qwindow=c(0,24), #time windows over which all variables are calculated; can be multiple windows for segmented analysis
  # for hourly analysis use qwindow=c(0:24),
  mvpathreshold =c(45, 101, 429),#needed if including bout metrics; can be multiple values: mvpathreshold=c(200, 250)
  mvpadur=c(1,5,10),
  boutcriter = c(0.8),
  bout.metric = 4,#see manual p35 (there are 6 options)
  M5L5res = 10,#time resolution of the M5L5 analyses in minutes (default=10 minutes)
  qM5L5 = c(0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9),#percentiles to be calculated over L5 and M5 window
  winhr = c(1,5,10), #mg during most and least active continuous x hrs of the day (continuous MX metrics) plus start time of 
  #these periods (can be < 1...so 0.5 would be 30 minutes); it can be multiple values: winhr=c(5, 10)
  ilevels = c(0,45,101,429,8000), #gives acceleration distribution by increments defined
  iglevels = TRUE,#IG calculated as described in original Rowlands et al. (2018)
  MX.ig.min.dur = 1,#IG calculated for least and most active continuous periods (in hours) set by 'winhr'.Minimum 'MX.ig.min.dur' 
  #value must be ≤ the lowest 'winhr' value, if < 10 hrs (otherwise, calculated by default)
  qlevels = c(
    480/1440, # most active 2/3rds of the day
    720/1440, # most active 12 h
    840/1440, # most active 10 h
    960/1440, # most active 8 h
    1080/1440, # most active 6 h
    1200/1440, # most active 4 h
    1320/1440, # most active 2 h
    1380/1440, # most active 1 h
    1395/1440, # most active 45 min
    1410/1440, # most active 30 min
    1420/1440, # most active 20 min
    1425/1440, # most active 15 min
    1330/1440, # most active 10 min
    1335/1440, # most active 5 min
    1338/1440, # most active 2 min
    1339/1440), # most active 1 min
  #these are the MX metrics (minimum acceleration (mg) for the most active accumulated X minutes); change the numerator &
  #denominator values, depending on qwindows duration (e.g., qwindows=c(7,23) for waking hours totals 960 minutes)
  na.rm=TRUE,


Thanks,
Liza
